The Grand Loop · Aug–Sep 2026 Route Day by day Moments Dining Budget Book now Practical
Bucharest → Venice Lagoon → Tuscany → Riviera → Provence → Beach Week → Rome → Dolomites → Arad

Twenty-four days.
Six countries.
One family story.

A village-to-village drive for M, his wife, Aria (8) and one well-travelled toy poodle: the cypress hills of Tuscany, a Michelin dinner on a lagoon island, castles above Monaco, the ochre canyons of Provence, five days of sand across two Tuscan coasts, the Colosseum at opening hour — and a Dolomites finale with friends.

24days · 12 Aug – 4 Sep
~5,700 kmmost days under 3 h
6countries + Monaco
12village-first bases, all pet-friendly
5full beach days · 2 coasts
Why this route

Every wish on the list, in the only order that makes the map work

With Spain stepping aside this summer (fires, and no workable ferry), the loop tightens beautifully: out through the Venice lagoon and Tuscany to the French Riviera and Provence, then back along Italy's two family coasts for the beach week, into Rome, and up to the Dolomites — no leg wasted, every night pre-checked for a small dog, and Arad reached late on 4 September, rested for the party.

01

Short drives, long afternoons

After the opening dash, most legs are 2–3 hours; you drive in morning light and every afternoon belongs to a pool, a beach or a village square. Exactly two mid-trip days stretch to ~5 h — Provence to Versilia, and Rome to Lake Garda — the toll for skipping Spain, paid twice, each split by a proper stop.

02

Villages, not cities

You sleep in Tihany, on the Cavallino peninsula, on a farm below Pienza, in Santa Margherita, La Turbie, Moustiers, Gordes, Marina di Pietrasanta, Castiglione della Pescaia, on Trastevere's quiet edge, by Sirmione's lake and in San Vito di Cadore. Florence, Monaco, Venice and Rome's centre are day raids — visit, then retreat.

03

A real beach week

Five consecutive swimming days, no compromises: Versilia's warm, waist-deep-forever sand under the marble Alps, then the Maremma's pine-backed Blue-Flag bays — bagno lunches, castle sunsets, and official off-leash dog beaches so every member of the family gets their holiday.

04

Art without museum fatigue

One anchor per region, none over 90 minutes: the Uffizi, a Riviera day from Miró's labyrinth to lunch under Picassos, Chagall or Matisse in Nice, Niki de Saint Phalle's mirror giants at golden hour, and the Colosseum at its 8:30 opening. Each visit short, booked ahead, and followed by ice cream.

05

Michelin nights, family-paced

You eat out once a day at most. The stars that remain are the right ones — a lagoon island, Montalcino's two-star estate, a Ducasse inn with a proper children's menu, Cortina's alpine agri-restaurant — plus the Colombe d'Or legend and a bookable three-star wild card in Menton.

06

Fixed points — and a poodle clause

Wednesday 12 Aug departure, Colosseum on 29 Aug (tickets release 30 Jul — alarm set), friends in the Dolomites 1–4 Sep, Arad late on the 4th, party on the 5th. And every single stay was re-checked to welcome a small dog, with fees and rules listed.

The route at a glance

A clockwise loop, folded by one night at sea

Day by day

The itinerary

Drive times are realistic motorway estimates with a break; add border/holiday margin. Stays show approximate August rates for the three of you — treat them as booking targets, not quotes. Dinner is listed only where it's an event; everywhere else, follow your nose.

Chapter I

The Dash West

Two long, purposeful days that spend the "big drive" allowance early — so the other twenty-two never have to. The poodle rides shotgun from km zero.
Wed 12 Aug · Day 1

Bucharest → Tihany, Lake Balaton

🚗 ~970 km · ~10 hStayAdler Hotel & Wellness, Tihany · ≈€140 · 🐩€10

The one honest slog of the outbound trip — leave by 6:30, cross the Carpathians on the A1, lunch near Deva, over the Nădlac II border and onto Hungary's motorways. By early evening you're descending to Lake Balaton's north shore.

  • Arrival reward: a warm-water evening swim — Balaton in August is 24–26 °C, and Aria gets to end a car day in a lake.
  • Tihany is a tiny lavender-scented peninsula village, not a resort town — exactly the pattern this trip follows.
Reception closes at 22:00 — tell the hotel you're arriving ~21:00 when you book (dog: €10/night, ≤15 kg — the poodle qualifies with room to spare). Vignettes: Hungarian e-vignette, rovinietă and Slovenia's e-vinjeta bought online the week before.
Thu 13 Aug · Day 2

Balaton → the Venice lagoon, dinner on a vineyard island

🚗 ~560 km · 5½ h⛴ 30 min vaporettoStayHotel Ca' di Valle, Cavallino · ≈€200 · 🐩 welcome⭐ Venissa — Michelin dinner in the vineyard

Coffee below Tihany's abbey, then the last push west: Slovenia's forests, a blink of Trieste's gulf, and by mid-afternoon you're checked in on the Cavallino peninsula — pool, garden, free parking, poodle officially welcome. Then the trip changes gear: park at Punta Sabbioni and step onto the Line 12 vaporetto.

  • Golden hour on Burano — the most colourful streets in Europe, with Aria leading and the poodle trotting the fondamenta (dogs ride the vaporetto free — leash and muzzle carried, or in her travel bag).
  • Dinner at Venissa on walled Mazzorbo next door — Michelin-starred, inside a vineyard growing a grape that survives on this island alone. The estate's casual Osteria Contemporanea is the same-vineyard fallback.
Venissa's five rooms were booked out — this mainland base is the fix. Romantic upgrade if the email gods smile: Casa Burano (same estate) sometimes grants 1-night stays — write to info@casaburano.it and get the pet OK in writing.
Chapter II

Tuscany — the hills you came for

Three nights on a farm above Pienza, in the heart of the UNESCO Val d'Orcia — pool with a view, dog in the garden, balloon at dawn.
Fri 14 Aug · Day 3

Venice morning, Florence art, Val d'Orcia by dusk

⛴ morning boat🚗 290 km · 3¼ h + 120 km · 1¾ hStayAgriturismo Palazzi del Papa, Pienza — 3 nights · ≈€280/night · 🐩€10/day

Two icons in one moving day — the only packed sightseeing day of the trip, and worth it. Early boat across the lagoon (or a slow Burano breakfast), then autostrada south.

  • Uffizi Gallery, mid-afternoon timed slot — with the split-duty system: one parent takes Aria in for 90 well-chosen minutes (Botticelli's Birth of Venus, da Vinci, Caravaggio's Medusa — under-18s free), while the other walks the poodle up to Piazzale Michelangelo for the skyline. Swap envy over gelato after.
  • Piazza del Duomo — the marble mountain of Brunelleschi's dome from the outside, then the golden drive south.
  • Arrive at the farm in time for a swim as the hills turn amber.
Florence has camera-enforced ZTL zones — park at Villa Costanza tram P+R or an Oltrarno garage and never drive the centre.
Sat 15 Aug · Day 4

The Val d'Orcia loop, slowly

🚗 ~50 km of lanes, no leg over 20 min⭐⭐ Campo del Drago — Ferragosto dinner

Ferragosto — Italy's summer holiday — so do as the Italians do: no ambitions, just beauty. A lazy triangle through the postcard villages, pool hours in between, poodle in the shade of the olive trees.

  • Pienza, the "ideal city" of Pius II — pecorino tasting, and the lane behind the Duomo with the valley falling away below.
  • Monticchiello — tiny, walled, and blissfully unbusy even in August; let Aria lead the lanes.
  • Bagno Vignoni — the village whose main square is a steaming Renaissance thermal pool.
  • Sunset at the Vitaleta Chapel lane — the most photographed two cypresses on Earth, ten minutes from your farm.
  • Ferragosto dinner, done properly: the valley's two-star at Castiglion del Bosco, 40 minutes through Montalcino wine country (see Dining) — it closes Sundays, so tonight is the night. The Rosewood estate is dog-friendly; ask about the restaurant, or the poodle guards the farm for the evening.
Estate lovers' footnote: two more Tuscan legends sit within reach — Monteverdi's restored hamlet is 25 min away (casual Zita serves daily, fine-dining Oreade Tue–Sat), and the Ferragamo family's Il Borro wine village lies an hour north (Osteria del Borro serves dinner nightly in August). Either works as a dinner swap.
Sun 16 Aug · Day 5

Sunrise balloon, Siena afternoon

🎈 ~1 h flight, dawn🚗 Siena 45 min each way🍝 Osteria La Porta — terrace lunch

The alarm hurts for exactly ten minutes — until the burner lights and the Tuscan hills unroll beneath the basket in first light. Your €350-per-person Siena quote matches Balloon Team Tuscany — and their child rules (from age 5, minimum one metre tall) mean Aria flies without the height worry. Prosecco (juice for her) and a farm breakfast on landing; ask the operator if the poodle can wait with the ground crew's chase vehicle.

  • Lunch on the tiny terrace of Osteria La Porta at Monticchiello's gate — pici with ragù and the valley shimmering below (book the terrace specifically).
  • Siena from 16:30, when the heat breaks: the shell-shaped Campo, the zebra-striped Duomo, the Gate of Heaven rooftop climb — dogs roam Siena's lanes happily, museums not, so tag-team the Duomo.
  • Evening stays light — pizza in San Quirico's piazza and an early night.
Chapter III

Two Rivieras

Italy's pastel fishing coast, then three nights in La Turbie village while Monaco glitters 500 m below.
Mon 17 Aug · Day 6

Tuscany → Santa Margherita, via the Leaning Tower

🚗 180 km · 2¼ h + 150 km · 1¾ hStayHotel Metropole, Santa Margherita — sea view · ≈€400 · 🐩€20 + pet menu

Roll out of the hills and stop 90 minutes in Pisa — the tower really does lean absurdly, and children from age 8 may climb its tilted spiral (book a slot; the non-climbing parent gets poodle-and-piazza duty). Hungry en route? A 30-minute detour lands you at Castelfalfi, the castle-village resort past San Gimignano — Il Rosmarino, its trattoria-pizzeria, is the family lunch pick (phone-confirm Monday hours, +39 0571 890159).

  • Arrive at the palm-lined seafront of Santa Margherita Ligure — your hotel greets the poodle with its own pet menu, no joke.
  • Evening in Camogli, 15 minutes over the headland: a vertical fishing village of trompe-l'œil facades the tour buses miss; swim off the pebble beach as the bell tower goes pink, dinner from whatever the boats brought in (see Dining).
Tue 18 Aug · Day 7

Abbey cove morning, ridge village by night

⛴ boat to San Fruttuoso🚗 210 km · 2½ hStayHôtel Napoléon, La Turbie — 3 nights · €615 total · 🐩€8/night

Before leaving Liguria, take the little boat to San Fruttuoso — a thousand-year-old abbey wedged into a cove reachable only by sea, where you swim above a submerged bronze Christ (ask the Golfo Paradiso boat crew about the poodle when buying tickets — leashed dogs usually ride). Then over the border to France by mid-afternoon.

  • Check into La Turbie for three nights — the stone village on the ridge above Monaco, exactly the pattern you asked for. The village's own Hôtel Napoléon holds all three nights in its Triple room (€615 total; dog €8/night).
  • Èze village at dusk — ten minutes along the Grande Corniche: when the day-trippers leave at six, the eagle's-nest lanes and the Jardin Exotique sunset are yours, no €2,000 room required.
Wed 19 Aug · Day 8

Monaco for the day, La Turbie for the night

🚗 15 min hops⭐⭐⭐ Mirazur, Menton — optional wild card

Monaco with an 8-year-old is a surprisingly great day. The poodle sits out the museum morning in the cool of your village room, and joins for the harbour afternoon.

  • Musée Océanographique — Cousteau's cliff-face aquarium palace; shark lagoon, touch tanks, whale skeletons on the terrace.
  • Changing of the Palace Guard at 11:55, then walk the F1 circuit's hairpin and tunnel — the barriers stay up all summer.
  • Golden hour at the Trophée d'Auguste back up in La Turbie, Monaco switching its lights on below.
  • Tonight's option for the ambitious: Mirazur in Menton, 20 minutes along the coast, open Wednesdays — if you're doing the three-star, this is its slot, since tomorrow's lunch is spoken for (see Dining).
Thu 20 Aug · Day 9

The Riviera art day — Mirós in a garden, lunch under Picassos

🚗 45 min west, hops on the way back🖼 lunch at La Colombe d'Or

The Côte d'Azur was the 20th century's studio, and today you drive straight into it. Forty-five minutes west, above the ramparts of Saint-Paul-de-Vence, the Fondation Maeght hides Miró's sculpture labyrinth and Giacometti's courtyard in a pine garden — an art museum that is effectively a treasure hunt for an 8-year-old.

  • Lunch at La Colombe d'Or — the inn where Picasso, Matisse and Léger paid for dinners with paintings that still hang over the tables; fig trees, white parasols, the Calder by the pool. Book it the way you'd book a starred table — and email ahead about the poodle on the terrace (French custom is on your side).
  • On the return through Nice's Cimiez hill, pick your master: the Chagall Museum or the Matisse Museum — five minutes apart, 40 minutes each is plenty. Both close Tuesdays — your Thursday is safe — €12 each, kids free.
  • Still fresh? Villa Kérylos at Beaulieu — a Belle-Époque recreation of an ancient Greek villa on the sea — is ten minutes below your village (daily to 18:00, €15 / €10, children's treasure-hunt audioguide with a diploma at the end). Otherwise: Fragonard in Èze and rosé at the Trophée.
Chapter IV

Deep Provence

Turquoise canyon water, a cliff village of faience stars, and the ochre badlands of the Luberon.
Fri 21 Aug · Day 10

Riviera → Gorges du Verdon → Moustiers

🚗 ~160 km · 2¾ h, scenicStayLa Bonne Auberge, Moustiers · ≈€130 · 🐩€13⭐ dinner at La Bastide (children's menu €25–40)

Climb away from the coast on the Route Napoléon into a different France — lavender stubble, thyme wind, and suddenly the Verdon: Europe's grandest canyon pouring impossible turquoise into Lac de Sainte-Croix.

  • Pedal-boat under the Galetas bridge into the mouth of the gorge — Aria captains, cliffs 300 m overhead, poodle as figurehead. Rentals right on the lake beach.
  • Moustiers-Sainte-Marie by evening: a village stitched to a cliff, with a gold star hung between the rocks by a returning crusader — find it from the terrace at dinner.
  • Dinner is still the Ducasse inn — La Bastide de Moustiers keeps its star and its children's menu, but takes no dogs, so you now sleep five minutes away at the village Logis (pool included) and the poodle digests her own dinner there while you eat yours.
Sat 22 Aug · Day 11

Canyon balconies → the Luberon

🚗 ~135 km · 2 hStayLe Mas des Romarins, Gordes · ≈€300 · 🐩€20

One or two Verdon rim viewpoints while the light is low, then west into the Luberon of Peter Mayle's books — dry-stone villages floating on vineyards.

  • Roussillon's Ochre Trail in late afternoon: a 45-minute walk through blood-orange cliffs and rust dunes — a natural playground for Aria (leashed dogs welcome).
  • Gordes at sunset — the whole stacked village turns the colour of honey; viewpoint on the D15 just before town.
Chapter V

The Beach Week — two coasts

Spain bowed out (fires, and no ferry) — so the five swimming days you asked for move to Italy's two family coasts: the endless soft sand of Versilia, then the pine-backed Blue-Flag bays of the Maremma. Buckets, spades, dog beaches.
Sun 23 Aug · Day 12

Sunday market, then east to the sand

🚗 ~465 km · 4¾ hStayHotel Joseph, Marina di Pietrasanta — 2 nights · ≈€285/night · 🐩 small dogs

Start at L'Isle-sur-la-Sorgue's famous Sunday antiques market on the water-wheel canal (8:30–9:45, dogs welcome, quick and early) — then the one long mid-trip day, back along the coast into Italy. It's the price of dropping Spain, paid once, with a Ligurian lunch stop halfway.

  • By 16:30 you're on Versilia's flat, warm sand — miles of it, with the marble Apuan Alps standing behind the beach umbrellas.
  • Evening passeggiata to the Forte dei Marmi pontile — the pier at sunset, focaccia in hand.
Mon 24 Aug · Day 13

Beach day I — the bagno ritual

🚗 zero — the car rests

Italy's beach-club culture, done properly: umbrella and loungers at a bagno, shallow shelf that stays waist-deep forever — the safest swimming of the whole trip for Aria — and a long pasta lunch with sandy feet.

  • The poodle has her own scene: Marina di Pietrasanta's dog-friendly bagni (Adua, Aretusa, Battelli) take leashed dogs on the sand; her swim windows are before 9:30 and after 19:00 — perfectly matching the humans' gelato schedule.
  • Evening in Pietrasanta, the sculptors' town 5 minutes inland — Botero's chapel frescoes, marble workshops, and the best people-watching piazza in Versilia.
Tue 25 Aug · Day 14

Down the coast to the Maremma

🚗 ~160 km · 1¾ hStayHotel L'Approdo, Castiglione della Pescaia — 3 nights · ≈€300/night · 🐩 all areas

One last Versilia morning swim, then a short hop south into wilder Tuscany: the Maremma, where pine forest runs to the water and Castiglione della Pescaia — a proper fishing village under a Pisan castle — earns its Blue Flag every year.

  • Afternoon on the town beach, 200 m from the hotel; evening climbing the old town's stone lanes to the castle walls for sunset over the harbour.
Wed 26 Aug · Day 15

Beach day II — and the poodle's best day of the trip

🚗 10 min hops at most

Nothing on the schedule but water. Morning at a bagno on the shallow town beach; late afternoon at one of Castiglione's three free official dog beaches — Selene, Rocchette or Punta Ala's Piastrone — where supervised dogs run off-leash on the sand from 8:30 to 19:30. Bring her vaccination booklet; bring Aria a bucket.

  • Aperitivo on the canal-harbour as the fishing boats come in; dinner is fritto misto in a paper cone or a proper seafood table — your call.
Thu 27 Aug · Day 16

Beach day III — with rainbow giants at golden hour

🚗 50 min south, late afternoon

Beach morning as usual — then, when the sun softens, the one art stop of the beach week and possibly Aria's favourite of the whole trip: Il Giardino dei Tarocchi, Niki de Saint Phalle's garden of house-sized mirror-mosaic tarot creatures (she lived inside the sphinx while building it).

  • Open 14:30–19:30, €15 / €10 for Aria — timed online tickets only, and the daily cap means booking ahead. The giants at golden hour, mirrors ablaze, are worth planning a week around.
  • Back for a late seafood dinner in the port.
Chapter VI

Rome — the arena and the alleyways

Three nights on the quiet edge of Trastevere, outside every ZTL camera zone, with a garage for the car and a sitter for the poodle on gladiator morning.
Fri 28 Aug · Day 17

Maremma → Rome

🚗 ~200 km · 2¼ hStayHotel Ripa Roma, Trastevere edge — 3 nights · from ≈€506 total · 🐩€20/stay

An easy hop down the Aurelia into the capital — your hotel sits on Trastevere's southern edge, verified outside the ZTL camera zones, with its own garage. Park once; the car doesn't move again until Monday.

  • First evening: cross into Trastevere's tangle of lanes — ochre walls, ivy, laundry lines — for a slow wander and an aperitivo in a cobbled piazza (the poodle will believe this city was built for her).
  • Gianicolo hill at sunset — all of Rome's domes at once, ten minutes' climb from dinner.
Sat 29 Aug · Day 18

The Colosseum, then dinner in the alleys

🎟 8:30 first slot — tickets release 30 Jul, 08:45🍝 Trattoria Da Teo — tables in the alleys

The day Aria has been promised. First slot of the morning at the Colosseum — coolest hour, thinnest crowds, gladiator ghosts at their most convincing — then the Forum and Palatine next door on the same ticket, before the heat wins.

  • Tickets are named and timed (€18, under-18s free but she needs her own reserved ticket; ID at the gate; bags max 30×40×15 cm). They release exactly 30 days ahead — Thursday 30 July, 08:45 — and August Saturdays go fast. This is the single most time-critical booking of the trip.
  • Dogs can't enter the Colosseum at all — a Rover sitter (Rome has hundreds, ~€20–25/day; book the meet-and-greet days ahead) takes the poodle for the morning.
  • Siesta through the furnace hours, pool of shade in the hotel courtyard — then the evening you asked for: dinner at a trattoria in the Trastevere alleyways, tables on the cobbles (see Dining).
Sun 30 Aug · Day 19

Rome on foot, gelato-paced

🚗 zero — tram 8 and sandals

The greatest-hits walk, early and outdoors — which conveniently is the most dog-friendly version of Rome: Pantheon at opening (one parent ducks in while the other holds the leash and a cornetto), Piazza Navona, the Trevi Fountain coin ritual, and the best gelato of the trip wherever the queue of locals says it is.

  • Afternoon: pedal-carts or rowboats in Villa Borghese's gardens — Rome's Central Park, poodle heaven.
  • Early night — tomorrow the mountains begin.
Chapter VII

North — Garda, then the Dolomites with friends

One castle-lake night to break the drive, then three nights in San Vito di Cadore below Antelao and Pelmo — two full mountain days, a hike for each, and the poodle welcome on the lifts.
Mon 31 Aug · Day 20

Rome → Lake Garda

🚗 ~500 km · ~5 h, split at OrvietoStayParc Hotel, Castelnuovo del Garda · €229 triple · 🐩€10

The second of the two long mid-trip days, broken cleanly at Orvieto — the cathedral town on its volcanic plug, 10 minutes off the autostrada, espresso with a view. By late afternoon: Lake Garda's southern shore.

  • Evening stroll in Sirmione — the Scaliger castle rises straight out of the lake with its drawbridge and swan moat; gelato on the ramparts-side promenade.
Tue 1 Sep · Day 21

Up into the Dolomites — San Vito di Cadore

🚗 ~250 km · 3 hStayHotel Marcora & Spa, San Vito — 3 nights · ≈€300/night HB · 🐩€15/day · phone to confirm

The Autostrada climbs past Belluno and the Dolomites' rock towers start filling the windscreen. Arrive mid-afternoon in San Vito, ten minutes below Cortina.

  • Aperitivo with your friends as Antelao — the "King of the Dolomites" — pinks up over the village at sunset.
  • Ambitions sorted over dinner: the turquoise Lago di Sorapis (pictured) hides 20 minutes away for the sure-footed grown-ups, but the two family days below are the plan.
Pet-friendly base is Hotel Marcora & Spa (~€15/day for the dog) — its online calendar was ambiguous for these dates, so this one is a phone booking: +39 0436 890651. Backups: Cima Belprà in San Vito, or Villa Blu in Cortina (dogs €20/night).
Wed 2 Sep · Day 22

Hike day — Tre Cime di Lavaredo

🚗 50 min to Misurina🥾 ~10 km loop · 3½–4 h · easy-moderate

The Dolomites' signature walk: the full circuit of the three great stone teeth, on wide military paths with rifugio stops for spremuta and strudel — lunch mid-hike at Rifugio Locatelli, facing the north walls. Fit eight-year-olds do it proudly, leashed dogs are welcome in the nature park, and early September means the summer crowds are gone.

  • Go early — the toll road needs a licence-plate reservation (book for today) and parking fills by 9.
  • Afternoon reward: Lago di Misurina's shoreline, then gelato in Cortina's Corso Italia on the way home.
Thu 3 Sep · Day 23

Emerald water, five towers, one farewell

🚗 Braies 1 h · Cinque Torri 30 min🚣 rowboat + chairlift + trench walk⭐ SanBrite, Cortina — farewell dinner

The grand finale, in three acts. At first light, Lago di Braies: take out a wooden rowboat before the day fills — emerald water, a wall of rock, the photo that hangs in your hallway. Be through the valley before the 9:00 road-restriction window (it runs to 15 Sep) or pre-book parking; boats go out from 8:00.

  • Act two, on the way back: the chairlift up to the Cinque Torri — dogs ride Cortina's lifts free (leash + muzzle) — five freestanding towers ringed by restored WWI trenches you walk straight through. Rifugio Averau, arguably the best mountain-hut table in the Alps, is 30 minutes' walk beyond if the group votes for a big lunch.
  • Act three: spa hour back at the hotel, then the farewell dinner with the whole group — Cortina's starred farmhouse if you book it (email about the poodle; otherwise she rests at the hotel), its casual sister farm if you don't (see Dining).
Chapter VIII

Home stretch

Fri 4 Sep · Day 24

San Vito di Cadore → Arad

🚗 ~1,000 km · 10–11 h with borders

The second and last permitted monster — but with the party on the 5th, a late-evening arrival on the 4th is exactly the plan. A civilised 7:30 start, out through the Cadore valleys to Lienz, then Villach – Graz – Budapest – Szeged and across at Nădlac: Arad by ~21:00 with proper lunch and coffee stops, in bed before midnight, fresh for tomorrow.

Keep the last Dolomites morning intact — Braies at dawn on the 3rd stays, and there's even time for a farewell breakfast with your friends on the 4th before rolling out.
Once in a lifetime

The moments this trip is really about

For everyone

A balloon over the Tuscan hills

Sunrise flight above the cypress lanes you fell in love with — one hour aloft, prosecco and farm breakfast on landing. Aria clears this operator's child rules with room to spare.

For Aria

The arena at opening hour

First slot of the morning in the Colosseum, gladiator ghosts still on shift — then the Forum before the heat wins.

For the grown-ups

A Michelin star on a vineyard island

Dinner inside Mazzorbo's walled vineyard, boats for taxis, Burano's colours across the footbridge.

For the album

Rowing on Lago di Braies

A wooden boat on glass-green water under a wall of Dolomite rock — earned by a dawn start, shared with your friends.

For Aria

Giants made of mirrors

Niki de Saint Phalle's house-sized tarot creatures blazing at golden hour — the artwork an 8-year-old files under "best place ever".

For everyone (poodle included)

Five days of sand, two coasts

Versilia's endless shallow shelf, then the Maremma's pine-backed bays — bagno lunches, castle sunsets, and official off-leash dog beaches.

For the grown-ups

Èze after the crowds leave

At 7 p.m. the eagle's-nest lanes empty out — golden stone, the exotic garden, the whole Riviera below. Ten minutes from your village bed.

For Aria

Captaining the Verdon

A pedal-boat under 300-metre cliffs into the mouth of Europe's grandest canyon, on water the colour of toothpaste.

Tables worth planning around

Michelin stars & honest legends

One meal out per day, remember — so these are the days when that meal is the event. Book the starred ones the moment dates firm up; children are welcome at every table below.

Venissa

★ MICHELIN
Mazzorbo island, Venice lagoon — dinner, Thu 13 Aug

Tasting menus built on lagoon fish, island vegetables and the walled vineyard around your table — a 30-minute vaporetto ride from your mainland base. Two blind tasting menus — €150 (7 courses) or €175 (10), ~2025 pricing — from chefs Chiara Pavan and Francesco Brutto, 1★ plus a green star for the estate's lagoon agriculture. One flag: 13 Aug is their first service after the summer break, so email to confirm — and the estate's own Osteria Contemporanea (open daily, à la carte, ~€45–70 pp) is the relaxed same-vineyard plan B that Aria may actually prefer, with garden tables the poodle can likely join (ask).

Closed Tue–Wed · dinner 19:30–21:00 · book at venissa.superbexperience.com the moment 2026 dates load · no published minimum age — mention Aria and the poodle by email (info@venissa.it).

Campo del Drago

★★ MICHELIN
Rosewood Castiglion del Bosco, Montalcino — dinner, Sat 15 Aug

The Val d'Orcia's own two-star, forty minutes through Brunello country from your farm: chef Matteo Temperini's Tuscan produce cooking inside a 1,700-hectare Montalcino estate. Dinner-only, closed Sun–Mon — which makes Ferragosto Saturday your slot.

Chef's menu €200 · 3 courses à la carte €180 · smart casual · no published minimum age — confirm Aria when booking (+39 0577 1913001) · the estate is dog-friendly with no pet fee; ask about the restaurant terrace, else the poodle keeps the farm.

Osteria La Porta

local legend
Monticchiello, Val d'Orcia — lunch, Sun 16 Aug

A tiny terrace at the gate of a walled village, pici with ragù and the valley shimmering below. The definition of a €40 meal you remember for years. Open daily in season, 12:00–15:00.

Book the terrace days ahead — Ferragosto weekend.

DaV Mare

Michelin Guide
Portofino piazzetta — dinner, Mon 17 Aug

The Cerea family (of three-star Da Vittorio) cooking Ligurian seafood on the world's most famous little square — open seven days in season, sharing plates made for families. Splashy, yes; unforgettable, also yes.

≈€100+ pp adults · book well ahead (Ferragosto week) · davmare.com · 30 min from your Santa Margherita hotel. Cheaper honest alternative: La Cucina di Nonna Nina in San Rocco di Camogli (phone-confirm Monday opening).

Mirazur — the wild card

★★★ MICHELIN
Menton — dinner, Wed 19 Aug (optional; lunch slots too)

Mauro Colagreco's garden-fed universe menu, once ranked the best restaurant in the world, 20 minutes from your La Turbie bed. As of late July, tables for three around your dates were still open — rare and tempting. A "Tribute to the Tomato" menu (€380) runs exactly from 18 Aug. Wednesday evening is its slot, since Thursday lunch belongs to La Colombe d'Or.

Universe menu €450 pp · closed Mondays in Aug · card guarantee, free cancellation until 15 days out · email reservation@mirazur.fr to confirm an 8-year-old and half portions. Skip guilt-free — the Moustiers inn two nights later has a star too.

La Colombe d'Or

the legend
Saint-Paul-de-Vence — lunch, Thu 20 Aug

Not a star — an institution. The inn where broke painters paid in canvases: you eat the famous hors-d'œuvres basket on a fig-shaded terrace with Picassos, Légers and a Calder mobile for company. The anchor of your Riviera art day.

No online booking exists — phone +33 4 93 32 80 02 or contact@la-colombe-dor.com 3–4+ weeks ahead for a summer terrace table · hors-d'œuvres platter €40, mains €22–65 (≈€70–110 pp) · open daily in season, families routinely at lunch · no published dog policy — ask when booking; French terraces are usually kind to small poodles · set Aria hunting for César's golden thumb.

La Bastide de Moustiers

★ MICHELIN · green star
Moustiers-Sainte-Marie — dinner, Fri 21 Aug

Alain Ducasse's Provençal farmhouse: the menu walks in each morning from its own 2,000 m² kitchen garden. Gentle, garden-side, and genuinely child-welcoming — the easiest starred dinner of the trip. The inn takes no dogs, so you now sleep at the village Logis five minutes away and the poodle sits this one out.

Menus €90–120 · children's menu €25–40 · last seating 20:30 · Friday is a normal service day · +33 4 92 70 47 47.

Trattoria Da Teo

Trastevere, in the alleys
Piazza dei Ponziani, Rome — dinner, Sat 29 Aug

Exactly the dinner you pictured: tables spilling onto a small cobbled piazza deep in Trastevere's lanes, cacio e pepe and carciofi done the Roman way, waiters who adopt children on sight. Takes phone bookings — decisive with an 8-year-old and a poodle under the table.

~€35–45 pp · open Saturdays (closed Sun) · +39 06 5818355 — call in the week of 17 Aug to confirm post-Ferragosto reopening · backup 300 m away: Da Enzo al 29 (no bookings — join the 18:45 queue; terrace noted dog-friendly) · seafood fallback: Osteria der Belli.

Rifugio Averau

gourmet hut · 2,413 m
Above Cinque Torri — lunch option, Thu 3 Sep

Named among the ten best mountain restaurants in the Alps: hand-made pappardelle and a 170-label cellar, reached by chairlift and a 30-minute walk. Fair warning for your one-meal rule: it shares the final day with SanBrite — let the group pick one, or declare the last day a two-table holiday.

Primi €15–17, mains to €32 · kids' pasta €15 · open to 25 Sep · dogs ride the chairlift free (leash + muzzle) · reserve by phone +39 0436 4660.

SanBrite

★ MICHELIN · green star
Cortina d'Ampezzo — farewell dinner, Thu 3 Sep

An "agri-restaurant" above Cortina: their own dairy, their own farm, spaghetti steeped in mountain-pine. The right full stop for the trip — with your friends around the table.

Menus €170 / €200 pp (whole table) · Thu is dinner-only; closed Wed · book via sanbrite.superbexperience.com and email ahead about Aria and the poodle · casual sister spot El Brite de Larieto is the fallback.

Book these now

The reservation checklist, in order of urgency

Thu 30 Jul, 08:45
Colosseum tickets for Sat 29 Aug — the one alarm-clock booking. Slots release exactly 30 days ahead at ticketing.colosseo.it (~08:45 CET). €18 adult, Aria free but needs her own named ticket; take the 8:30 first slot; ID required at the gate. August Saturdays go fast — be on the site when it opens.Miss it and resellers charge €29+ — or shift the visit to Sunday morning (releases 31 Jul).
Book now
The availability-checked stays — these all showed live rooms for your exact dates this week: Adler Tihany (12 Aug, dog €10), Hotel Joseph Versilia (23–25), L'Approdo Castiglione (25–28), Hotel Ripa Roma (28–31, from ≈€506 total), Parc Hotel Garda (31 Aug, triple €229) and Hôtel Napoléon — book the "Triple 3 lits" category, €615 for all 3 nights (the balcony/family rooms are missing the last night, which is why you only saw two).Availability moves daily in August — lock these first.
Phone calls
Two bookings need a human voice: Hotel Marcora, San Vito (+39 0436 890651 — pet-friendly base for 1–4 Sep; its online calendar is ambiguous, backups: Cima Belprà / Villa Blu Cortina) and Hotel Ca' di Valle, Cavallino (+39 041 968017 — quote-based booking for the 13 Aug lagoon night).Both accept small dogs; get the pet confirmed in the same call.
Emails, in writing

Sunrise balloon, Siena — your €350 pp quote matches Balloon Team Tuscany; children fly from age 5 and one metre tall, so Aria is comfortably in. Book 15 or 16 Aug with the other morning as weather spare, and ask if the poodle can wait with the ground crew.Free cancellation windows vary — check when paying.

Practical

Small print that saves the day

🪪 Paperwork before you leave

  • Passports/IDs valid well past September; carry them to the Colosseum (named tickets, checked at the gate).
  • Car: green card / insurance confirmation, EU breakdown cover, spare bulbs & vests.
  • Vignettes — buy online the week before: Hungary e-vignette, Slovenia e-vinjeta (outbound), Austria vignette (return). Romania rovinietă as usual.
  • France Crit'Air sticker: Nice's low-emission zone is active in 2026 (weekdays 8:00–20:00, camera-enforced, foreign plates fully in scope). Order only at certificat-air.gouv.fr (~€5 shipped abroad), 4–6 weeks before departure; the email receipt is interim proof.
  • EHIC/CEAM health cards — and the poodle's EU pet passport (see her card →).

🐩 Travelling with the poodle

  • EU pet passport: microchip + rabies vaccination at least 21 days old at departure (booster before expiry needs no new wait). No tapeworm treatment needed on this route.
  • Italy's rule: leash max 1.5 m in public and carry a muzzle at all times — it must be worn on public transport (vaporetto, trams) and on Cortina's lifts, where dogs otherwise ride free.
  • Where she can't go: Colosseum, Uffizi, the museums, the balloon — that's what split-duty, hotel siestas and the booked Rome Rover sitter are for.
  • Where she'll thrive: Castiglione's three free off-leash dog beaches (8:30–19:30, vaccination booklet required), Versilia's dog-friendly bagni (her swim slots: before 9:30 / after 19:00), leashed on the Tre Cime loop, free on the Cinque Torri chairlift.
  • August rule zero: never, ever the parked car — even "just five minutes". Water bowl lives in the daypack.

🚗 Driving quirks by country

  • Italy ZTL: camera-enforced historic-centre zones in Florence, Siena, Pisa — and Rome. Your Rome hotel sits verified outside the ZTL polygons with its own garage (€25/day): park once, use tram 8 and taxis (small dogs ride both; muzzle on the tram).
  • Motorway tolls: Italy ≈ €150–180 across all Italian legs (the beach-and-Rome loop adds autostrada km); France ≈ €40–60. Hungary monthly e-vignette ≈€28 covers both crossings.
  • Trastevere's daytime ZTL runs 06:30–10:00 Mon–Sat; night gates are usually suspended in August — but your outside-the-zone base makes it academic.
  • Fuel up before Alpine passes and before Hungarian borders (cheaper in Slovenia/Hungary than Italy/Austria).

🌡 August realities

  • Rome will hit 33–36 °C: arena and Forum at 8:30, siesta 13:00–17:00, dinner at 20:30 like the Romans.
  • 15 Aug is Ferragosto — Italy's biggest holiday. Your itinerary spends it on farm + villages; book that weekend's tables and rooms first. Many Rome trattorias close mid-Aug — hence the reopening phone-check.
  • Water shoes for pebbly Camogli; rash vests save sunscreen wars; the Versilia and Maremma shelves are blissfully shallow for a young swimmer.
  • Lago di Braies water is ~10 °C even in September. Rowing yes, swimming... heroic.

🎒 The Aria toolkit

  • Museum pacing: 90 minutes max, one "mission" per visit (find Medusa at the Uffizi, count Miró monsters at Maeght, find César's golden thumb at lunch, spot the she-wolf at the Forum).
  • Audiobook + playlist stack for the two long days; offline maps downloaded for the whole route.
  • Booster seat required everywhere on this route; EHIC card; a small sketchbook — from Burano's colours to the Tarot Garden's mirrors, this route begs to be drawn.

⏱ Timing traps

  • Colosseum tickets release exactly 30 days out (Thu 30 Jul, ~08:45 for your Saturday) — the only booking with an alarm clock attached.
  • L'Isle-sur-la-Sorgue market is Sunday morning — arrive by 8:30, leave by 9:45; it's a long driving day.
  • Tarot Garden opens 14:30 only, timed tickets, daily cap — book the 27 Aug slot ahead.
  • Cortina: the Braies road is restricted 9:00–16:00 through 15 Sep (reserve at pragsparking.com or arrive before 9:00); Faloria and Tofana lifts run to 20/27 Sep, the Cinque Torri chair to 11 Oct — dogs free on all of them, muzzle carried.
  • Campo del Drago closes Sun–Mon (hence the Ferragosto-Saturday booking); SanBrite closes Wednesdays and does dinner-only Thursdays — your farewell slot.

💶 Money notes

  • Bagno economics: umbrella + two loungers runs ~€25–45/day in Versilia, less in the Maremma — book front rows ahead in August.
  • France: the €25–35 lunchtime menu du jour is how you eat brilliantly on non-event days.
  • Italy: agriturismo dinners (your Pienza farm does them) are the best-value fine food in the country; coperto on every bill is normal.
  • Pet fees run €8–20/night at your stops — ~€150 across the trip, the cheapest happy traveller aboard.

The Grand Loop · 12 August – 4 September 2026

Built for M, his wife, Aria and the toy poodle — Bucharest → Balaton → Venice lagoon → Val d'Orcia → Liguria → La Turbie → Provence → Versilia → Maremma → Rome → Lake Garda → San Vito di Cadore → Arad.

Prices, opening hours and pet policies were researched in July 2026 and are approximate; availability signals were checked in late July 2026 and move daily in August — always confirm at booking. Drive times are motorway estimates without long stops; August traffic and borders can add 10–20%.
